record.paper_title: Problem collection from the IML programme: Graphs, Hypergraphs, and Computing
record.context_brief: Edge deletions to bipartite structure in K_r-free graphs
record.original_question: How many edges must be deleted from an n-vertex K_r-free graph in order to make it bipartite?

evidence.quote: Question 9.5. How many edges do we need to delete to make a Kr-free graph G of order n bipartite?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For integers $r \geq 3$ and $n \geq 1$, let $G$ be a simple graph on $n$ vertices that contains no copy of the complete graph $K_r$ as a subgraph. Define $f_r(G)$ to be the minimum number of edges whose deletion from $G$ yields a bipartite graph, and let
$$f_r(n) = \max\{f_r(G) : G \text{ is a } K_r\text{-free graph on } n \text{ vertices}\}.$$
Determine $f_r(n)$ (asymptotically as $n \to \infty$). In particular, for each $r \geq 3$, find the smallest constant $c_r$ such that every $K_r$-free graph on $n$ vertices can be made bipartite by deleting at most $c_r n^2 + o(n^2)$ edges.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is a long-standing question of Erdős. For $r=4$, Sudakov (2007) proved that every $K_4$-free graph on $n$ vertices can be made bipartite by deleting at most $n^2/9$ edges, with the extremal graph being the balanced complete tripartite graph, settling Erdős's conjecture in this case. For $r=3$, Erdős conjectured the optimal bound is $n^2/25$ (achieved by the balanced blow-up of $C_5$); this remains open, with the best known upper bound around $n^2/23.5$, improving earlier $n^2/18$ bounds. The general case for $r \geq 5$ remains open.

status_evidence.title: Making a K_4-free graph bipartite (Sudakov)
status_evidence.snippet: Every K_4-free graph G with n vertices can be made bipartite by deleting at most n^2/9 edges. Moreover, the only extremal graph is the complete 3-partite graph with parts of size n/3. This proves an old conjecture of Erdős.
status_evidence.claim: The r=4 case is solved: tight bound n^2/9.

status_evidence.title: Making a triangle-free graph bipartite (Erdős problems)
status_evidence.snippet: Erdős conjectured that every triangle-free graph on n vertices can be made bipartite by removing at most n^2/25 edges; extremal example is a blow-up of C_5.
status_evidence.claim: The r=3 case (Erdős's n^2/25 conjecture) is still open.

status_evidence.title: Max Cuts in Triangle-free Graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Improved bound: every triangle-free graph can be made bipartite by removing at most n^2/23.5 edges.
status_evidence.claim: Best known upper bound for r=3 is roughly n^2/23.5, still above the conjectured n^2/25.
